2 Chronicles 33.summary: Manasseh establishes foreign altars, practices divination and desecrates the temple. The LORD warns him and the people, but they do not listen. Assyrian commanders take him captive; in distress he humbles himself and prays, and the narrative reports his restoration. He removes foreign gods and repairs defenses, though the people still sacrifice at high places. Amon succeeds him and continues evil, before being assassinated. The chapter focuses on manasseh’s evil, repentance and restoration and locates these events within the Chronicler’s account of Israel and Judah’s worship, kingship and relationship with the LORD.

2 Chronicles 34.summary: Josiah begins seeking God while young and later removes idolatrous sites. During temple repairs Hilkiah finds the Book of the Law, which Shaphan reads to the king. Josiah grieves and sends representatives to Huldah, who announces coming judgment yet acknowledges the king’s humility. Josiah publicly reads the covenant and urges the people to follow it. The chapter focuses on josiah restores the temple and finds the law and locates these events within the Chronicler’s account of Israel and Judah’s worship, kingship and relationship with the LORD.

2 Chronicles 35.summary: Josiah sponsors a major Passover with extensive provisions, priestly service and Levitical participation. 2 Chronicles 36.summary: After Josiah, Judah has a rapid succession of kings under Egyptian and Babylonian pressure. The narrative recounts widespread unfaithfulness and rejection of prophetic warnings. Babylon destroys Jerusalem and the temple and exiles survivors. It closes with Cyrus of Persia authorizing return to Jerusalem to rebuild the LORD’s house, an ending that points toward restoration. The chapter focuses on judah falls; cyrus announces return and locates these events within the Chronicler’s account of Israel and Judah’s worship, kingship and relationship with the LORD.
